newsitem.title: USA: CBOT details proposed wheat delivery changes.
newsitem.headline: CBOT details proposed wheat delivery changes.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade unveiled a proposal to expand the commercial delivery options for its wheat futures contract at Toledo and St Louis as a way to counter declining storage capacity at Chicago elevators.
The exchange said in a statement that the changes, based on a unanimous vote of the CBOT's Wheat Task Force, will be considered by the CBOT Board of Directors in April.
Subject to a Board vote and approval by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and CBOT membership, the changes would go into effect with the September 1999 wheat futures contract, it said.
The changes in delivery include -
--Expansion of the Toledo delivery point.
--Changing the Toledo price differential from -2 cents a bushel to par.
--Specification of shipping certificates (backed by warehouse receipts) as delivery instrument for warehouses in the St Louis switching district.
--Allowing delivery from off-water warehouses in St Louis.

The proposed changes come on the heels of significant changes in the delivery system for CBOT corn and soybeans, passed by the Board and to be voted on by the membership on April 15. Those changes include dropping St Louis and Toledo as delivery points in favor of Illinois River elevators.
Both sets of changes have been driven by CFTC concerns about possible market manipulation in delivery periods due to declining elevator capacity at the CBOT's traditional points.
Details of proposed specifications for the wheat contract:

--Delivery in Chicago and Burns Harbor, Indiana, and in the Toledo district defined as Wood, Lucas, Seneca, and Fulton counties and Fostoria in Ohio and Monroe County in Michigan. Delivery in St Louis, East St Louis and the Alton, Illinois, switching district.
--Delivery at Chicago, Burns Harbor and Toledo at par. Delivery in St Louis at an 8-cent a bushel premium.
--Delivery by federal warehouse receipt in Toledo, Chicago and Burns Harbor and by shipping certificates in St Louis.
--Storage charge of $0.0012 per bushel per day.
--Delivery at par for Grade Number 2 SRW, HRW, DNS, NS. Delivery at 3 cents premium for Grade Number 1 of same.
--Only SRW deliverable at St Louis.
--Maximum certificates allowed to issue: Registered daily rate of loading of not less than 3 barges times 30.
--Each certificate must be backed by federal warehouse receipt.
((Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8720))
